chunks: He said: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, may God have mercy on him, reported to me from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his uncle Ya'qoob ibn Salim, from Abu al-Hasan al-Abdi, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both.
He said: A servant does not restrain himself for the sake of God except that God will admit him into Paradise.
And may God's blessings be upon our master Muhammad, the Prophet, and his family, and peace.

key_terms.الجنة: Paradise - the ultimate reward for those who practice self-control
key_terms.على الله: For the sake of God - dedicating self-restraint to divine obedience
key_terms.يحبس نفسه: Restrains himself - the act of controlling one's temptations and desires

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for controlling one's temptations according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) quotes a teaching that a servant who restrains himself for the sake of God will be rewarded with entry into Paradise. This short hadith emphasizes self-discipline and controlling one's desires as a path to divine reward, reflecting the broader ethical emphasis on nafs (self) purification in Shia tradition.
word_analysis: may Allah have mercy on him

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 5. He said: Abul Qasim Ja’far ibn Muhammad, may Allah bless him with mercy, reported to me from his father, from Sa’d ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from ‘Ali ibn Asbat, from his uncle Yaqoob ibn Salim, from Abul Hasan al-Abdi, that: Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him,
said: "A slave of Allah does not control his temptation for the sake of Allah, except that Allah rewards him by entering him into Paradise."
And may Allah bless our master Muhammad, the Prophet and his progeny.
